entities.name: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church (Amharic: የኢትዮጵያ ኦርቶዶክስ ተዋሕዶ ቤተ ክርስቲያን, Yä-Ityop'ya Ortodoks Täwahedo Bétä Kristiyan) is one of the world's oldest Christian churches — claiming connection to the 4th-century mission of Frumentius (ordained by Athanasius of Alexandria in approximately 330 CE), making Ethiopia one of the world's first Christian nations, while tradition also traces roots to the eunuch of Queen Candace baptized by Philip the Evangelist (Acts 8) — representing a Christian tradition that has maintained unbroken institutional continuity for approximately 1700 years.

Ethiopian Christianity has unique characteristics distinguishing it from both Western and Eastern Orthodox traditions: the Ethiopian Bible includes 81 books (including books not found in Catholic, Protestant, or Eastern Orthodox canons, such as 1 Enoch and Jubilees — texts that were preserved in Ethiopia when lost elsewhere), the Ark of the Covenant is traditionally held at Axum's Church of Our Lady Mary of Zion, Saturday is observed as Sabbath alongside Sunday worship, dietary laws similar to Jewish kashrut are observed, and the church has had intimate connections with Ethiopian statecraft through the Solomonic dynasty's claims of descent from Solomon and the Queen of Sheba.

The Tewahedo Church (Tewahedo meaning 'unified' in Amharic, referring to its non-Chalcedonian Miaphysite Christology) was autocephalous from 1959 and was intimately connected to imperial Ethiopian identity — Emperor Haile Selassie was the last Solomonic dynasty emperor, whose overthrow by the Derg in 1974 radically altered the church's state relationship. The church also inspired the Rastafari movement (which regards Haile Selassie as divine).

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church — one of Christianity's oldest national churches, preserving unique ancient texts, inspiring Rastafari globally — is historically significant as one of the world's most ancient Christian traditions and a monument to Ethiopian civilization's extraordinary cultural heritage.
